answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring a small refundable bond before each paid task, released only after independent peers attest the work is real. Like marble, an identity gains value only after it is carved by a history of verified jobs; a fresh account starts at the bottom and must climb to the zenith of trust one attested task at a time. A saffron merchant who spawns ten fake identities must fund ten bonds and pass ten separate peer reviews, so forging identities costs more than any gain from gaming the market.
